value.body: Doctors in pharmaceutical companies and contract research organisations (CROs) work as medical advisors, medical monitors in clinical trials, and physicians in pharmacovigilance (drug safety). The work involves reviewing trial data and adverse-event reports, supporting regulatory submissions and giving medical input to product teams, rather than treating patients.

items.label: Typical roles
items.value: Medical advisor, medical monitor, drug-safety physician

items.label: Indian trial rules
items.value: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019

items.label: National drug-safety system
items.note: Run by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An MBBS with registration is the base. Some roles take freshers, especially in pharmacovigilance and medical writing; medical-advisor roles often prefer an MD (pharmacology or a clinical subject) or clinical experience. Short certificates in clinical research or Good Clinical Practice (GCP) are common but not legally required.

value.title: At a glance
items: It trades patient care and night duties for office hours and corporate career ladders.
Work is concentrated in a few cities with pharma and CRO hubs.
Moving back to clinical practice later can be harder if skills lapse.
